title: Free-Floating Subdivisions: Names of Places
scope: Topical, chronological, form, and area subdivisions usable on a free-floating basis, within the limits of the usage notes, under geographic place names (continents, regions, islands, countries, states, counties, cities, extinct cities, city sections, metropolitan/suburban areas, regions based on cities, geographic features and designated areas, bodies of water, U.S.-recognized tribal jurisdictions); not under celestial bodies, non-jurisdictional international organizations or corporate bodies, or agencies controlling parks
general_notes: LC practice: As stated in H 1075, LC catalogers will no longer use form subdivisions. Instead assign an appropriate term or terms from Library of Congress Genre/Form Terms (LCGFT), e.g. *Textbooks*. To replace a form subdivision that includes a demographic group, also assign Library of Congress Demographic Groups Terms (LCDGT) to bring out the audience of the resource being cataloged, e.g. *German speakers* or *Arabic, Students of*.

Chronological subdivisions: In 1997 restrictions were lifted on use of subdivisions of the type *--16th*, [*17th*, *18th*, *19th*, *20th*, *21st*] century under *--Civilization* and *--Intellectual life*, thereby allowing their use under geographic headings at any level. At the same time, subdivisions of the type *--16th*, [*17th*, *18th*, *19th*, *20th*, *21st*] century were added under the subdivisions *--Economic conditions*; *--History*; *--History, Military*; *--History, Naval*; *--Politics and government*; *--Social conditions*; and *--Social life and customs*. These free-floating century subdivisions should be used with caution under names of countries and other geographic entities where chronological subdivisions for specific time periods have been established. Assign these century subdivisions only where there is no conflict with chronological subdivisions established in the subject authority file.
For additional subdivisions used only under names of bodies of water, streams, etc., see H 1145.5.
Section G (Areas and regions) entries are free-floating geographic phrase headings formed from city names or geographic features (consult H 790), not subdivisions appended with --.
